$comment: Advisories the CI security gate is allowed to ignore. See scripts/audit-gate.mjs.
An entry belongs here ONLY when there is no published fix to upgrade or
override to, AND the vulnerable code path is unreachable from this app.
If a patched version exists, pin it via `overrides` in package.json instead —
Every entry needs an `expires` date. On that date the gate starts failing
again, forcing a re-evaluation. That is deliberate: this file must not become
a place where advisories go to be forgotten.

allow.title: React Router: RSC Mode CSRF Bypass Allows Action Execution Before 400 Response
reason: No published fix exists. The advisory names 8.3.0 as the first patched
version, but react-router-dom has never published ANY 8.x release —
latest is 7.18.2 across all dist-tags (checked 2026-08-01). There is
nothing to upgrade to and nothing to pin via `overrides`. npm's only
proposal is a downgrade to 7.11.0, which discards seven minors of fixes.
The vulnerable code path is unreachable here. The advisory is in RSC
server-action handling; this client is a plain SPA — client/src/App.tsx
uses BrowserRouter, and there is no @react-router/dev, @react-router/node
or @react-router/serve anywhere, no RSC mode, no server actions, no
framework mode. The version matcher flags us on range alone.
Review on expiry: if react-router 8.3.0 has shipped, upgrade and delete
this entry (that is a semver-major with breaking route-API changes — see
LIF-215). If it still has not, re-confirm the SPA-only assumption above
